column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1 on SDK 20.5.17, update 1.0.1; 73,512 shaders, all translated. Its shader libraries are in the IoStore container, Oodle-compressed shader groups that the port
# decodes with the game's own Oodle on the device (porter device_ue: one round, 5,919 groups, 74,244 shaders in 44 s), so the port needs the device connected.
# Tested 2026-11-06 on the Legion Y700 (TB322FC, Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, Android 16), docked (1920x1080): the brightness setting, the title, a new game (difficulty), the
# opening cinematic, the first road (walking, tutorials), the cutscene, the first battle's command menu; an autosave, and Continue from it after a restart (many times).
# 60 fps (the profile's fps_target): frame work p50 about 16.5 ms, GPU 10-13 ms in the field and the cinematic, 0-6 dropped frames per 300; 0 audio underruns; no red line.
# Its sprite particles' parameters (R32F buffer textures of 36-44 elements at offsets not a multiple of Adreno's 64) are read from an aligned copy (gfx_vk_tex.c vk_tbuf_view).
# Its particle compute shaders write R32UI / R32I buffer textures through float images: those get an integer variant (gfx_vk_shader.c spv_int_images), and the battle's
# haze and dust sprites (vertex shader fb570ef861debd17) draw since.
# Not drawn: the fires in the first battle's background that the battle tutorial's picture shows. Likely by design on this platform, not proven on a Switch: every blended
# draw of the battle frame was identified with DM_VK_X_FLAT_VS (in env.txt: pipelines made before it keep their state) and none is a flame: fb570ef8 the haze sprites,
# 1300ca45ddca3566 / c55d54c8f41b1520 ground-fog volumes, 70eb4102 the moon's glow (pass 22), 1bbd4f87bfa7cdf5 light shafts and 6a4e114179eda634 a screen effect (pass 24,
# after depth of field). The fire light (not a Niagara effect) is there. The game's Switch device profile holds fx.Niagara.QualityLevel at 1 (Min and Max 1 at main+0x779eb70 /
# 0x779eb80 / 0x779eb90 at run time; 3 in the binary) and fx.Niagara.PruneEmittersOnCook is 1, so emitters of higher quality levels are left out of its packaged data; the
# binary is the original Switch's (no Switch 2 model query among its imports), and the tutorial pictures may come from another platform. Ruled out on the port's side: the
# GPU count readback, occlusion (only timestamps and SAMPLES_PASSED, answered as visible), the frame rate (DM_FPS_TARGET=30), handheld mode, Niagara's culling switches
# (visibility, distance, instance count and global budget culling written to 0 from the title, main+0x779eca8 / 0x779ecac / 0x779ecb0 / 0x779ec74, with DM_CTL pokei).
# The game ignores command-line console variables (a shipping build: -dpcvars and -ini: through DM_GAME_ARGS_ADD changed nothing, r.ScreenPercentage included).
